executive_brief: The football-match-manager spec defines a full-stack TypeScript application using React 18 on the frontend and Node.js 18 with Express on the backend, backed by PostgreSQL 14 with an ORM layer. It outlines testing with Jest, React Testing Library, and Supertest, authentication via OAuth 2.0/Passport.js with JWT session handling, football data integration through a cached REST client, and UI styling via Tailwind CSS or Material‑UI. The stack targets a scalable, maintainable web app for tracking matches and user followings.

architectural_constraints: Jest as the unit/integration testing framework
React Testing Library for frontend tests
OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect for third‑party login
JWT or encrypted cookies for secure session management
Redis or in‑memory caching layer to reduce football API calls
React Context API for managing authentication and followed matches state
Tailwind CSS utility‑first or Material‑UI component styling
Passport.js with Google, Facebook, and Apple strategies
Rate limiting and retry mechanisms for football data API requests
ORM abstraction (Sequelize/TypeORM) for database interactions and migrations
Secure session practices: HTTPS, secure cookies, CSRF protection
Normalization of external API responses to internal data models
Storage of minimal user data (ID, email, name) linked to followed matches

maturity_assessment: The specification captures a coherent technical stack and clear non‑functional choices, yet it lacks defined goals, functional requirements, scope boundaries, and open questions. These omissions represent high‑severity gaps that prevent the spec from being actionable for implementation, indicating the project requires further refinement before development can proceed. Status: REFINEMENT.
critical_dependencies: OAuth 2.0 SDKs for Google, Facebook, Apple
Mandatory unit test execution via Jest before code merge
